([[Montverde, Florida]]) | college = [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] (2013–2015) | draft_year = | draft_round = | draft_pick = | draft_team = | career_start = | years1 = | team1 = | highlights = * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2013 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2013]]) | medal_templates = {{MedalSport | Men's [[basketball]]}} {{MedalCountry|the {{USA}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA Under-17 World Championship|FIBA World U17 Championship]]}} {{MedalGold| [[2012 FIBA Under-17 World Championship|2012 Lithuania]] | [[United States men's national basketball team|National team]]}} }} '''Dakari Johnson''' (born September 22, 1995) is an American basketball player who recently closed his college career at the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|University of Kentucky]]. ==High school career== Considered a five-star recruit by [[ESPN.com]], Johnson was ranked as the No. 2 center in the nation in 2013.[http://espn.go.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/119182/dakari-johnson Dakari Johnson Recruiting Profile] ==College career== On January 5, 2013, Johnson committed to [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]]. He joined [[Julius Randle]], twins [[Andrew Harrison (basketball)|Andrew Harrison]] and [[Aaron Harrison]], [[James Young (basketball)|James Young]], and [[Marcus Lee]] as one of six Kentucky signees to be selected in the [[2013 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]] as well as the [[Jordan Brand Classic#2013|2013 Jordan Brand Classic]]. On April 23, 2014 UK announced that Johnson planned to return to Kentucky for his sophomore season. He joined another top-notch incoming freshman class including [[Karl Towns]], [[Trey Lyles]], [[Devin Booker]], and [[Tyler Ulis]]. On April 9, 2015 Dakari along with Kentucky teammates [[Aaron Harrison]], [[Andrew Harrison (basketball)|Andrew Harrison]], [[Devin Booker]], [[Trey Lyles]], [[Karl-Anthony Towns]], and [[Willie Cauley-Stein]] all declared to enter their names into the [[2015 NBA Draft]] forgoing his final 2 years of eligibility. ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/dakari_johnson_862048.html Kentucky Wildcats bio] {{Persondata | NAME = Johnson, Dakari | ALTERNATIVE NAMES = | SHORT DESCRIPTION = American basketball player | DATE OF BIRTH = September 22, 1995 | PLACE OF BIRTH = [[Brooklyn, New York]] | DATE OF DEATH = | PLACE OF DEATH = }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Johnson, Dakari}} [[Category:1995 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:African-American basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players at the 2014 NCAA Men's Division I Final Four]] [[Category:Basketball players at the 2015 NCAA Men's Division I Final Four]] [[Category:Basketball players from New York]] [[Category:Centers (basketball)]] [[Category:Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball players]] [[Category:McDonald's High School All-Americans]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Brooklyn]] {{1990s-US-basketball-bio-stub}}
